sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Detroit, Michigan?
sections.html:
Selling in Detroit means working in a city where block-by-block conditions differ more than the city name suggests. Detroit covers about 139 square miles of land on the Detroit River, and a house in Boston-Edison or Indian Village sells in a very different market from a modest bungalow on the east side, even though both sit in the same city and the same county.

The Census Bureau estimates 649,095 residents for July 2025, up from 639,111 at the 2020 count. That follows decades of decline from a 1950 peak of 1.85 million, and the city's own 2013 bankruptcy filing ended in 2014. Local buyers, investors and out-of-state landlords all shop here, so a seller usually gets a mix of owner-occupant and investor interest.

Detroit is the seat of Wayne County, and the county handles the deed recording and the older delinquent tax accounts. Many sale questions end at the Wayne County offices, even when the house is inside the city limits.

sections.h2: How does the Detroit housing market compare in Census numbers?
sections.html:
Detroit has the lowest median home value and the lowest owner-occupancy rate of the four Michigan cities in this comparison. Half of Detroit households rent, which shapes who is likely to buy your house.

A median value of $83,900 against a median gross rent of $1,074 explains why investors keep a close eye on Detroit sales. The same figures also mean that repair costs can eat a bigger share of a sale price here than in Dearborn, where the median value is $218,800.

sections.h2: What kinds of houses and neighborhoods do Detroit sellers have?
sections.html:
Most of the city is low-rise. Outside downtown and New Center, Detroit consists mainly of single-family houses and small buildings. Pre-war working-class areas have wood-frame and brick houses, while Brush Park, Woodbridge, Indian Village, Palmer Woods and Boston-Edison hold larger, more ornate homes. The city lists 42 structures on the National Register of Historic Places.

The terrain is flat. Detroit slopes gently from northwest to southeast on glacial and lake clay, with the Detroit Moraine, a broad clay ridge only about 62 feet above the river, under the older parts of town. Clay soil and a cold climate matter to a buyer's inspector:

  • Winters stay at or below freezing on an average of 44 days a year, so heating systems, roofs and pipes get a close look.
  • Summers pass 90 degrees on about 12 days, which puts attention on cooling and attic ventilation.
  • Clay ground under older neighborhoods makes basement moisture and foundation drainage fair questions from a buyer's inspector.

Fix or price these items before listing, because they are the ones that renegotiate contracts.

sections.h2: Which employers, schools and transit options help Detroit buyers?
sections.html:
The Detroit Medical Center is the city's largest single employer, joined in Midtown by Wayne State University and the Henry Ford Health System in New Center. General Motors, Rocket Mortgage, Ally Financial and DTE Energy have headquarters in the city, and about 80,500 people work downtown, roughly one-fifth of the city's employment. Tenants and buyers who work in those districts look for housing close to them.

The Detroit Public Schools district is the largest in Michigan, and the city has a large charter sector alongside it. Many families also look at suburban districts, so ask your agent how school boundaries affect the buyer pool on your street.

Transit includes DDOT buses, the QLINE streetcar, the downtown People Mover loop, and SMART service to the suburbs. Detroit also has four border crossings to Windsor, including the Gordie Howe International Bridge that opened in 2026. Detroit Metropolitan Airport serves the region.

sections.h2: What state taxes and fees apply when a Detroit house sells?
sections.html:
The seller owes the state transfer tax. It is $3.75 for each $500 of value under MCL 207.525, and the county adds 55 cents per $500 in a county below 2,000,000 residents under MCL 207.504. Ask the Wayne County Register of Deeds which county rate applies on your deed date. The tax is due to the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed is delivered, and the grantor is the party liable under MCL 207.523.

MCL 207.526 exempts several transfers. These include deeds given to a child or grandchild, a deed in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure, court-ordered transfers without a stated price, and land contracts where legal title has not yet passed. A foreclosure deed is exempt, but a later sale by the lender is not.

  • The buyer files a transfer notice with the assessor within 45 days (MCL 211.27a).
  • Taxable value resets to state equalized value the calendar year after the sale.
  • You should ask the Detroit assessor for the form that ends your principal residence exemption.

For current-year and past-due bill amounts, ask the City of Detroit Office of the Assessor and the Wayne County Treasurer for written payoff figures before you sign anything.

sections.h2: Why does tax foreclosure timing matter for Detroit sellers?
sections.html:
The Wayne County Treasurer runs the county's annual auction of tax-foreclosed properties. The minimum bid is a fixed figure that includes the treasurer's foreclosure and auction expenses, winners must pay in full within 72 hours, and the office records a quit claim deed within 30 days of the auction closing. Selling before the auction lets you choose the buyer and the price. Ask the treasurer what redemption rights remain on your parcel.

If you owe back taxes, ask the Wayne County Treasurer's office for the payoff and any payment plan options right away, and ask whether the closing agent can pay the balance from your proceeds. A sale that closes with taxes cleared is easier for a buyer's lender to approve than one with an open lien.

sections.h2: How do your options compare for a Detroit house that needs work?
sections.html:
Listing with an agent can reach owner-occupant buyers who finance with a mortgage, but lenders and appraisers look hard at condition, and repair requests follow. A sale to an investor trades some price for speed, and an as-is contract can set who handles trash, personal property and open utility accounts.

Whichever route you choose, compare offers by net proceeds. Subtract the transfer tax, unpaid taxes, any lien payoff and the cost of repairs you would otherwise perform. Ask each buyer for proof of funds and a closing date in writing.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax when I sell a house in Detroit?
faqs.a: The seller. State law makes the grantor liable for the tax, which is $3.75 per $500 of value at the state level plus a county amount. Some deeds are exempt, including transfers to a child or grandchild.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Detroit house that has back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Ask the Wayne County Treasurer for a payoff figure, and have the closing agent pay the balance from your sale proceeds. Selling before the county's foreclosure auction lets you keep the equity that remains.

faqs.q: What happens to the property tax bill after a Detroit sale?
faqs.a: The buyer's taxable value resets the year after the sale to the state equalized value, which is half of the assessor's estimate of market value. The buyer must report the transfer to the assessor within 45 days.

faqs.q: Do I have to fix my Detroit house before selling?
faqs.a: Buyers and their lenders often ask for repairs, and the contract decides who pays. Ask the City of Detroit for any local compliance requirements that apply to your property type, particularly if it is a rental.

faqs.q: How many people live in Detroit?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 649,095 residents as of July 1, 2025. Median home value for 2020-2024 is $83,900 and about half of homes are owner-occupied.
